rop_whom_to_screen.text: Gestation 34-36 weeks with speciﬁed risk factors* or an unstable clinical course

rop_whom_to_screen.text: *Signiﬁcant cardiorespiratory support, prolonged/poorly controlled oxygen therapy, signiﬁcant anemia, blood transfusion, sepsis, poor postnatal weight gain

rop_treatment_indications.text: Zone I: Any stage with plus disease, or stage 3 without plus
Zone II: Stage 2-3 with plus disease
Reactivation/signiﬁcant PAR after anti-VEGF; stage 2–3; stage 4–5
Advanced ROP (Stage 4-5): Requires referral for surgery
Treatment-requiring ROP should be treated urgently, preferably within 48-72 hours of the decision to treat

rop_clinical_dos.text: Ensure timely ROP screening and follow-up
Document the date and place of next screening in discharge card
Counsel the family regarding need for follow-up and risk of vision loss if screening is delayed

rop_clinical_donts.text: DO NOT discharge/transfer an at-risk neonate without a documented ROP follow-up plan
DO NOT delay referral/treatment when indicated
DO NOT stop ROP follow-up without advice of ROP-trained ophthalmologist

rop_kpis.text: ROP screening coverage (%) = Eligible infants who received at least one ROP eye examination x 100 / Total eligible infants for ROP screening
Timely ﬁrst ROP screening (%) = Eligible infants screened within the recommended ﬁrst-screen window x 100 / Eligible infants due for ﬁrst screening
All SNCUs/NICUs should periodically assess the KPIs and undertake quality improvement measures to achieve 95-100% compliance

1. High likelihood of preterm birth within the next 7 days due to any one:

ancs_eligibility.text: Planned preterm birth for maternal/fetal indication

ancs_eligibility.text: 2. Gestational age assessed accurately, preferably by early USG
3. No clinical chorioamnionitis or systemic maternal infection
4. Adequate childbirth care is available at the facility or at the referral facility
5. Adequate preterm newborn care be ensured(including CPAP) at the facility or the receiving facility
IMPORTANT: Start ACS promptly once eligibility criteria are met, even if the full course may not be completed before birth

ancs_kpis.text: ACS coverage = Women at 24+0–33+6 weeks identiﬁed with high likelihood of preterm birth who received ≥1 ACS dose × 100 / All women at 24+0-33+6 weeks identiﬁed with high likelihood of preterm birth (Target: ≥80%)

hypo_monitoring_schedule.text: *in IDM, monitoring can be stopped between 24-36 hours provided feeding is established
Infants on IV ﬂuids: Every 6-8 hours

hypo_symptoms.text: LOOK FOR THE FOLLOWING SYMPTOMS AND SIGNS
Episodes of cyanosis, apnoea or tachypnoea

hypo_recheck_1h.text: If BG ≥ 45 mg/dL: Continue feeds; Continue BG monitoring 6 hourly for 24 hours
Start IV glucose infusion if: BG < 45 mg/dL OR Symptoms develop

hypo_increase_gir.text: Increase GIR by 2 mg/ kg/min (maximum 12 mg/kg/min)
hypo_increase_gir.label: BG < 45 mg/dL

hypo_persistent_refractory.text: Persistent (GIR requirement >3-7 days) or Refractory (GIR > 10-12 mg/kg/min for 24 hours) hypoglycemia
Consider ENDOCRINE/ METABOLIC disorders & REFER to higher centre

hypo_euglycemic_wean.text: Euglycemic for 24 hours on IV ﬂuids
hypo_euglycemic_wean.label: BG ≥ 45 mg/dL

hypo_euglycemic_wean.text: Reduce GIR by 2 mg/ kg/min every 6 hours

hypo_dos.text: Monitor BG in all; as per protocol

hypo_donts.text: Do NOT substitute dextrose solutions for breastmilk
Do NOT separate a stable mother-infant dyad solely for glucose monitoring
Do NOT give antibiotics for hypoglycemia unless sepsis is suspected

hypo_kpis.text: Blood glucose screening coverage = At-risk neonates monitored for BG as per protocol × 100 / Total at-risk neonates eligible for BG monitoring (Target ≥90%)
Timely BG re-check after treatment = Hypoglycemic episodes with repeat BG within prescribed interval × 100 / No. of hypoglycemic episodes treated (Target ≥90%)

hypo_neuro_followup.text: NEONATES WITH SYMPTOMATIC, SEVERE, RECURRENT OR PERSISTENT HYPOGLYCEMIA SHOULD RECEIVE STRUCTURED NEURODEVELOPMENTAL FOLLOW-UP

hypo_asymptomatic_branch.text: Breastfeeding or a measured volume of expressed breastmilk (Formula milk if EBM not available) by paladai or gavage

hypo_symptomatic_branch.text: IV bolus: 2 ml/kg of 10% of dextrose slowly over 1 minute
Start IV infusion of dextrose at a glucose infusion rate (GIR) of 6 mg/kg/min

triage_initial_assessment.text: Attach temperature probe and pulse oximeter
Assess for emergency signs using TABC & CD
T: Temperature; A: Airway; B: Breathing; C: Circulation; C: Coma/convulsions; D: Dehydration
Classify into EMERGENCY, PRIORITY or NON-URGENT based on signs given below

triage_kpis.text: Neonates with a documented triage category at initial assessment
triage_kpis.label: Triage classification documented (%); All neonates assessed × 100

triage_kpis.text: Sick neonates with temperature, SpO₂ AND blood glucose recorded at initial assessment
triage_kpis.label: Complete triage measurements (%); All sick neonates assessed × 100

triage_abbreviations.text: IDM: Infant of a diabetic mother

kmc_continue_while_on.text: Phototherapy (interrupt only during treatment, resume immediately)
Twins: individually or together, depending on stability and caregiver availability

kmc_dos.text: Start KMC early in every eligible preterm or low-birth-weight baby; continue as long as possible
Ensure correct positioning, a clear airway, and secure support; monitor temperature, breathing, and feeding
Support exclusive breast milk feeding and counsel families to continue KMC at home with scheduled follow-up

kmc_donts.text: Do not initiate KMC in babies unable to breathe spontaneously after resuscitation, in shock, or requiring mechanical ventilation
Do not routinely stop KMC for oxygen, CPAP, IV therapy, or tube feeding
Do not delay KMC because the mother is unavailable; involve a trained alternate caregiver

kmc_kpis.text: No. of neonates initiated on KMC x 100
kmc_kpis.label: KMC coverage among eligible neonates = Total eligible neonates during that period; Target: ≥90%

kmc_kpis.text: Neonates receiving KMC for ≥8 h per 24h x 100
kmc_kpis.label: Percentage of eligible neonates getting > 8 hours of KMC = All neonates receiving KMC; Target: ≥80%

rd_diagnostic_criteria.text: Presence of ANY ONE: RR ≥60/min; Chest retractions; Nasal flaring; Grunting

rd_immediate_actions.text: Apnoea/gasping, poor effort or shock: Stabilize immediately; ventilate when indicated
Maintain TABC; provide warmth; admit to SNCU/NICU
Attach pulse oximeter; monitor HR, RR, SpO₂ and CRT; assess SAS
Feed when stable: breastfeed if mild RD; OG feeds when appropriate on CPAP; decompress stomach
Withhold feeds; give IV fluids for severe RD, recurrent apnoea, poor perfusion or abdominal concerns

rd_algorithm_overview.text: *If GA is uncertain, BW ≤1800 g may be used as an operational surrogate

rd_initial_preterm_cpap_caffeine.text: CPAP 5–6 cm H₂O; blended oxygen; titrate FiO₂ to SpO₂ 91–95%
Caffeine citrate for babies <34 weeks requiring respiratory support, as per protocol

rd_initial_term_moderate_severe_cpap.text: CPAP 5–6 cm H₂O; blended oxygen; titrate FiO₂ to SpO₂ 91–95%
Caffeine citrate for babies <34 weeks requiring respiratory support, as per protocol

rd_initial_term_mild_nasal_o2.text: If SpO₂ <91%: 0.5–1 L/min; Titrate to SpO₂ 91–95%

rd_reassessment_sepsis.text: Monitor SpO₂ continuously while on oxygen/CPAP
Reassess clinical status, SAS and FiO₂ requirement within 15–30 min of starting/changing support
Reassess at least 1 hourly while on respiratory support; immediately if any worsening

rd_improving.text: Decreasing SAS; SpO₂ 91–95% on stable/reducing support; Comfortable breathing

rd_surfactant_indication.text: Suspected worsening RDS in a preterm neonate <34 weeks, AND FiO₂ >0.30 on CPAP ≥6 cm H₂O to maintain SpO₂ 91–95%
Give promptly when indicated—before established CPAP failure

rd_outcome_improving_weaning.text: Comfortable breathing; no significant apnoea; low oxygen requirement
Reduce FiO₂, then CPAP as per protocol
Trial off when stable on CPAP 5 cm H₂O and FiO₂ 0.21–0.25
Monitor SpO₂ for 24 h after stopping

rd_outcome_not_improving_optimize_cpap.text: If on Nasal Prongs oxygen, rising oxygen need or distress: Start CPAP
Check prongs, circuit and delivered pressure
Increase CPAP up to 7–8 cm H₂O; Titrate FiO₂

rd_cpap_failure_referral.text: Persistent hypoxaemia/rising FiO₂ despite optimized CPAP, recurrent apnoea, shock or fatigue
Escalate support; intubate/ventilate when indicated; stabilize and refer urgently

rd_clinical_dos.text: Assess severity using SAS; monitor SpO₂ continuously
Start CPAP within 30 min of identification of indication
Give early rescue surfactant promptly when indicated

rd_clinical_donts.text: Do NOT give unmonitored supplemental oxygen
Do NOT order routine CBC/CRP, chest X-ray or blood gas in uncomplicated mild RD
Do NOT give IV fluids, antibiotics or blood products routinely
Do NOT delay ventilation or referral when CPAP fails
